repo_model.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search candidate workspace. The root candidate loads a configured task, emits task-family-specific NumPy predictions, and is evaluated by an isolated grader against the official validation metric.

entrypoints.how_to_run: python main.py --debug for the fast pipeline check, or python main.py for the full run.

evidence.description: Defines the fidelity, fraction, and seed arguments.

where_to_edit.role: Primary solution entrypoint: replace the trivial prediction logic with feature construction, training, tuning, and task-specific inference.

evidence.description: Explicitly instructs replacing the baseline with a real solution.
Contains the central task-family prediction dispatch.

where_to_edit.role: Contract-aware helpers for loading sanitized RelBench data, saving both prediction files, checking temporal safety, and evaluating MAP@K locally.
Preflight validator for prediction files, shapes, finite values, binary ranges, and recommendation dtypes.

evidence.description: Checks both validation and test prediction files.
Validates recommendation shapes and integer dtypes.

where_to_edit.role: Immutable orchestration and scoring code; do not modify it.

evidence.description: Instructs candidates not to modify kapso_evaluation.
Identifies grader.py as the complete immutable scoring pipeline.

claims.statement: The candidate reads dataset/task identity from environment variables, loads the RelBench task with download disabled, sizes the validation and test splits, and detects rolling snapshots from the cached validation table.

evidence.description: Documents rolling snapshots with an empty validation table.
Computes validation row count and rolling mode.

claims.statement: Prediction generation dispatches by task family: recommendations receive a tiled integer ranking, binary classification receives 0.5 probabilities, multiclass classification receives uniform class scores, and remaining task types receive the training-target median.

evidence.description: Falls through to the regression-style median prediction.

claims.statement: The candidate writes NumPy prediction files into KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR; ordinary runs write both validation and test predictions, while rolling invocations write the per-tick test prediction for later assembly.

evidence.description: Writes validation predictions outside rolling mode.
Prints prediction shapes and run mode.

claims.statement: The immutable grader runs main.py in an isolated subprocess, validates prediction artifacts, computes official RelBench validation metrics, archives full-fidelity runs, and emits the machine-readable score manifest.

evidence.description: Maps fidelity to main.py or main.py --debug.

claims.statement: Rolling evaluation runs the candidate once per snapshot with a snapshot-specific cache, reads each tick's indices and test predictions, and reconstructs the official row-order vectors.

evidence.description: Creates an isolated stage for each snapshot.
Sets the snapshot-specific cache and output directories.

claims.statement: Every ordinary run must produce val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy with rows positionally aligned to the RelBench validation and test tables; validation predictions must be out-of-sample.

evidence.description: Requires both files after every run and positional alignment.
Requires validation predictions to be out-of-sample.

claims.statement: Prediction formats are task-dependent: binary and regression use float vectors, multiclass uses an N-by-C float array, and recommendation uses an N-by-K integer ranking of distinct destination IDs within the valid destination range.

evidence.description: Defines binary, regression, and multiclass formats.
Defines recommendation shape, dtype, and ID requirements.
Checks recommendation shape and integer dtype.

claims.statement: Candidate data access must use the sanitized, read-only RelBench cache with download=False; test labels are unavailable and must not be probed.

evidence.description: Requires RelBench API access with download=False.
States that the cache is read-only and test labels are absent.

claims.statement: The search score is the official primary validation metric; test metrics are private and cannot be used to select or tune a candidate.

evidence.description: Defines the official validation primary metric as the search score.
States that test metrics are private.
Computes validation metrics from the validation predictions.
Places the primary validation metric in the manifest score.

claims.statement: Time-aware feature construction must not use rows after the seed timestamp; assert_temporal_safety raises when such rows are present.

evidence.description: Detects rows whose time exceeds the seed time.

claims.statement: Run python main.py --debug as the mandatory fast end-to-end pipeline check, then run python main.py for the full training path.

evidence.description: States that the harness runs the program twice.

claims.statement: After predictions are written, run python kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py; successful validation prints OK for each split followed by all checks passed.
For official scoring, invoke the grader with --fidelity fast or full; both fidelities score the complete validation split, and the final manifest exposes the official score.

evidence.description: States that the scored item set never shrinks.

claims.statement: Rolling snapshots have zero validation rows; main.py consequently suppresses val_predictions.npy for each tick, while the grader only requires per-tick test predictions and assembles the final vectors afterward.

evidence.description: Documents empty validation tables in rolling snapshots.
Sets rolling when the validation row count is zero.
Skips validation output in rolling mode.
Assembles the final vector from tick predictions.

claims.statement: The current main.py does not implement a separate debug algorithm: --debug is only reflected in the log, although the grader uses it to identify fast fidelity.

evidence.description: Uses --debug only in the diagnostic output.

claims.statement: The shipped candidate is deliberately a baseline rather than a learned solution: recommendations are fixed IDs, classifiers are constant distributions, and the fallback target prediction is the training median.

evidence.description: Identifies the file as a baseline candidate.
Instructs replacing it with a real solution.

claims.statement: The local checker warns rather than fails when recommendation IDs are out of range or duplicated, so a passing check does not make an invalid ranking contract-compliant.

evidence.description: Only warns about out-of-range recommendation IDs.
Requires valid destination IDs and ranked outputs.

claims.statement: The runtime requires Python with relbench and numpy installed; the candidate directly imports both packages.

evidence.description: States that Python with relbench and numpy is sufficient.

claims.statement: The candidate requires RELBENCH_DATASET, RELBENCH_TASK, RELBENCH_CACHE_DIR, and KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR; the grader additionally supplies primary-metric, timeout, work-directory, and shared-cache configuration.

book.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search candidate workspace. The root candidate loads a configured task, emits task-family-specific NumPy predictions, and is evaluated by an isolated grader against the official validation metric.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: A root candidate script feeds contract-compliant predictions into an isolated RelBench scoring harness.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the root candidate directly or invoke the provided grader for official scoring.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Modify the root candidate and use the starter-kit helpers; treat the evaluation suite as immutable.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Prediction artifacts, data access, temporal scope, and scoring must follow the evaluation contract.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Use debug execution, the prediction preflight checker, and the official fast grader to validate changes.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: The starter candidate is intentionally trivial and rolling/debug behavior differs from a normal full invocation.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: The workspace depends on Python, NumPy, RelBench, and harness-provided environment configuration.
